approach.method_basis: The Parent learns a recurrent SMILES language model from an unlabeled molecular corpus and starts each objective with a fresh policy copied from that frozen prior. Each accepted batch contributes its best-scoring half. A memory retains the thirty-two strongest earlier elites, and the strongest eligible historical records join the current examples with their original strings and scores. Within history, an example's weight decreases with the number of earlier fitting batches that used it. The total current and historical loss shares remain proportional to their row counts. The policy fits weighted squared errors toward frozen-prior log likelihood plus sixty times accepted reward, takes up to twelve clipped Adam steps, and retains the final policy. It directly samples complete SMILES, with chemical validation and canonical duplicate rejection refilling each batch.
approach.novelty: Add gradient-norm balancing between the current and historical learning groups. At the start of each history-bearing update, measure the current mean-loss gradient and the historical gradient after the Parent's exposure weighting. Set the two loss shares inversely to those gradient norms, then hold the shares fixed for the update. Each group therefore starts with the same gradient contribution magnitude, while history keeps its existing relative weights. The measured Parent usually lets the current group dominate despite stronger historical rewards. Earlier siblings changed which histories train, their within-group exposure weights, residual penalties, target ceilings, checkpoint retention or historical displacement protection. This mechanism changes the balance between the two group gradients before the unchanged optimizer acts. Equal contribution does not guarantee useful historical information: it can greatly reduce learning from fresh molecules or reinforce repetition. Actual gradient and proposal evidence will determine whether that tradeoff helps.

hypothesis: At each history-bearing adaptation update, set fixed current and historical loss shares inversely to the norms of their respective starting mean-loss gradients, with the historical gradient retaining the Parent's normalized inverse-exposure weights, so the two groups have equal starting contribution magnitudes; preserve selected members, augmented targets and the inherited optimizer.

finding_summary.headline: Balancing changed learning, but group-gradient reconstruction failed and every seed lost final score.
finding_summary.insights:
The first historical intervention isolates a useful tradeoff before the sampled trajectories diverge. On identical starting examples and likelihoods, average final current-group error was 41.85 with balancing versus 29.32 with the Parent, while historical error was 18.88 versus 23.33. Current fitting was worse in thirteen of fifteen matched sessions. More historical influence can therefore buy better average historical fitting while weakening learning from the fresh batch; it is not a general protection guarantee. Across the later child stream, historical group error still rose in 71 updates and 817 individual historical exposures worsened. History received more than 99% of the loss in 21 nonterminal updates, and the effective selected batch shrank from 9.19 to 5.82 rows on the same selected inputs.

The score loss is not explained by a universal absence of chemical variety. Accepted core counts fell for three objectives but rose slightly for median-2 and sitagliptin. The molecular assessment finds that sitagliptin remains broadly diverse while failing to reproduce useful compact polar arrangements consistently; its largest score loss occurs despite 783 distinct cores versus 775 before. Docking already reaches coherent cyclic-amine chemistry near the numerical ceiling. Familiar rings, higher validity and improved replay fitting do not by themselves produce useful new molecular combinations. The same recurrent representation still generates oversized tails, questionable linkages and unspecified stereochemistry. Positive, unattainable historical targets also remain common: 627 exposures versus 489 in the Parent, on their different sampled streams.

This rules out failure to change coefficients or gradient direction as the explanation for lost utility. It also shows that scalar balance is an insufficient success criterion. Exact group-vector reconstruction remains open: real backward agreement establishes which objective executed, but cannot explain the systematic disagreement with the separately summed gradients. The saved evidence cannot determine whether that numerical discrepancy contributed to the score loss. Any interpretation that stronger historical influence is beneficial must now account for both the observed loss of fresh-batch fitting and increased repetition, as well as this unresolved numerical behavior.
finding_summary.results:
The fixed-share mechanism reached the real optimizer. In all 420 history updates followed by proposals, the measured starting contribution imbalance fell from 0.7012 on average to at most 4.59e-8. History received 84.54% of the loss mass on average. Every update changed the direct gradient direction even after clipping, and all 450 real first backward passes matched the direct actual objective exactly. Original accepted targets, selected-member rules, within-history exposure ratios and the fifteen history-free first-proposal controls remained intact.

One registered numerical check failed systematically: the direct balanced gradient did not reconstruct from the separately measured group gradients within the stated tolerance in any of the 435 history updates. Relative discrepancies reached 0.283% in nonterminal updates and 0.413% in terminal updates, compared with the approximately 0.001% registered tolerance. This limits the claim of exact vector reconstruction; it does not erase the observed scalar balance, changed direct gradient or real optimizer execution.

After history fitting, raw duplicate draws increased from 37.38% to 57.67%, canonical-novel yield fell from 54.80% to 37.62%, and batches needing further sampling increased from 29 to 90. All fifteen evaluations nevertheless completed their 300-call budgets. Mean final Top-1 fell from 0.517655 to 0.493672, a paired change of -0.023983. Seed changes were -0.004895, -0.009276 and -0.057779. The largest task loss was sitagliptin, whose mean endpoint fell from 0.287161 to 0.169219. Mean recorded AUC rose from 0.406769 to 0.423980, mainly alongside faster docking progress, so better average early discovery did not deliver the predicted final-score gain.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich aromatic chemistry reaches coherent cyclic amines, but retains narrow analogue families, oversized tails and unspecified stereochemistry.
molecular.overall_character: This assessment reads every supplied trajectory for node n-95c3f5710341 and Parent n-3462511d7ff0: all five objectives and seeds 0, 1 and 2, with 900 recorded molecules and 870 accepted optimizer proposals per objective in each panel. No objective lacks trajectories. The counters describe accepted optimizer strings, not rejected raw generations or experimentally isolated compounds. In the fixed task order, ring-closure presence rates are 0.9977, 0.9966, 0.9954, 0.9908 and 0.9839; aromatic-atom presence rates are 0.9885, 0.9943, 0.9885, 0.9575 and 0.9425. These are molecule-level text-presence rates, not fractions of atoms that are aromatic. A passive RDKit reading gives median heavy-atom counts of 24, 32, 27, 23 and 24 and median ring counts of 3, 4, 4, 3 and 3. Phenyl and heteroaromatic rings, amides, sulfonamides, ethers, nitriles and saturated nitrogen heterocycles are all represented. Distinct atom/bond-specific Bemis-Murcko core counts are 425, 315, 506, 735 and 783, versus Parent counts 472, 372, 537, 733 and 775. Thus the complete output is structurally broad, while several high-scoring seed streams concentrate on close analogues. Core counts do not measure usefulness. Many leading structures use conventional medicinal-chemistry bonds, but imidates, activated alkenes, acylhydrazones, unusual sulfur connectivity, overgrown peptide-like structures and long alkyl appendages make the whole set only questionably plausible. All accepted structures parse in the matching RDKit environment; that establishes representation validity, not synthesis, stability, exposure or biological activity. Explicit tetrahedral and double-bond stereochemical notation is absent throughout both panels despite potentially stereogenic structures. Passive descriptor methods, source hashes and all seed comparisons are retained in runs/SPIRAL2/policy/responses/r0011-09-improve-L03-molecular-audit/audit.json and stereo.json. Score interpretations below are associations within the supplied molecules; they do not infer an unseen target structure or mechanism activation.

per_task.generated_character: The accepted set is dominated by compact aromatic amides: median 24 heavy atoms, with nitriles in 255 of 870 proposals versus 7 in the Parent. Seed 1 develops diaryl cyanoacrylamides with acetanilide or imidate substituents. Its cited maximum has 24 heavy atoms, two benzene rings, two carbonyls and a nitrile. Seed 0 instead reaches an N-ethyl methylpyrazole carboxamide attached to fluorobiphenyl, also with 24 heavy atoms, and related heteroaromatic lactam/carboxamides. Seed 2 keeps methoxy-substituted indole and benzimidazole families carrying an aryl amide or benzyl nitrile. These are recognizable small-molecule frameworks, although the imidates and activated alkene require more chemical scrutiny than ordinary aryl amides. The Parent maxima were predominantly three-ring pyrrole, aryl-ether and diarylamine carboxamides. Current versus Parent recorded maxima by seed are 0.492632 versus 0.490235, 0.495261 versus 0.447421, and 0.447848 versus 0.476731. The chemistry changes differently in each seed rather than uniformly acquiring a missing ring class.
liabilities: The cyanoacrylamide is an electrophilic conjugated alkene, and aryl imidates introduce hydrolytic and tautomeric questions. These are structural concerns, not measured reactivity or stability.
Repeated amide-rich growth, a permanently charged bulky peptide-like molecule and densely functionalized polycycles create large synthetic and physicochemical burdens.
There are 108 accepted proposals with RDKit-perceived unassigned tetrahedral centres, while the digest stereocentre-notation rate is 0.0.
missing_features: Consistent preservation of the compact aromatic, nitrogen-containing envelope is missing from the low-scoring tail; both excessive growth and nitrogen-free fragments occur. The data do not establish an obligatory unseen fused-ring scaffold.

Productive variation beyond the repeated diaryl activated-alkene core is limited within seed 1: 53 of its 58 highest-scoring accepted proposals share one atom/bond-specific Murcko core. Ring chemistry is available, but useful alternative attachment arrangements are unevenly explored.

Defined alkene geometry is missing from the cyanoacrylamides; defined tetrahedral stereochemistry is missing from more complex off-family products. The score evidence does not establish a benefit from specifying either.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The cited 24-heavy-atom acetanilide/cyanoacrylamide reaches 0.4952605565, whereas a 50-heavy-atom quaternary-ammonium peptide-like proposal scores 0 and the 59-heavy-atom repeated indole-amide/guanidine structure scores 2.7846374431e-48. Compactness is associated with the better observations, but is not sufficient: the nitrogen-free, 16-heavy-atom cyclic alcohol scores only 0.0107671849. Seven digest maxima score identically despite aryl positional changes and replacement of an acetanilide linkage by an imidate. This suggests limited discrimination among those compositionally similar arrangements, not evidence that the imidate has equal chemical quality. The initial trimethoxyindole carboxamide scores 0.3051048084; late seed-2 benzimidazole/benzyl-nitrile and related indole-amide examples score 0.4355405789 and 0.3410994870. A ring-rich but enlarged 33-heavy-atom late product drops to 5.3229519627e-06. The observed gradient favors a compact aromatic heteroatom/carbonyl arrangement over indiscriminate ring or chain growth.

per_task.generated_character: These are the largest typical proposals in the panel: median 32 heavy atoms and four aromatic rings, with halogen text in 0.7138 of accepted strings. Seed 0 builds four-ring amino-azine/heteroaryl systems with benzylamine links, aryl nitriles and sometimes trifluoromethyl groups. The maximum is a 33-heavy-atom triazine-bearing structure with nine nitrogen atoms, including three nitriles, and no oxygen. Seed 1 develops extensively substituted quinoline/oxazole/aryl ethers. Seed 2 instead concentrates on methoxy/hydroxy aza-aromatic acylhydrazones carrying fluorinated or brominated benzoyl groups. The final cited examples in that seed have three aromatic rings and 32-38 heavy atoms. The azine, ether and amide linkages are conventionally accessible in principle; multiple regioselective substitutions and acylhydrazone geometry complicate that general plausibility. Compared with the Parent, nitrile-bearing proposals rise from 31 to 214 and sulfonamides fall from 160 to 19. The Parent seed-0 high end included extended alternating nitrogen linkages; its seed-1 high end was also an amino-azine family, and seed 2 used aryl sulfonamides with imine-bearing extensions. Current versus Parent maxima are 0.615587 versus 0.589985, 0.607304 versus 0.618622, and 0.605208 versus 0.608588.
liabilities: Large aromatic surfaces, multiple halogens and closely related nitrile-rich substituent patterns can create solubility and selectivity concerns; neither property was measured here.
Acylhydrazones bring possible E/Z mixtures and hydrolytic sensitivity, and some products repeat that linkage rather than introducing a distinct stable framework.
The low-scoring thiocarbonyl-to-sulfone linkage and isolated silicon-oxygen fragment illustrate that a valid representation can still be chemically unusual for this molecular context.
missing_features: The most productive amino-azine and aryl-nitrile arrangement is absent from the lower-scoring sulfone-rich examples, despite similar aromatic ring content. Ring count alone misses the relevant attachment chemistry.

Alternative coherent linkers and ring connectivities are poorly represented within the late acylhydrazone family: 57 of the 58 highest-scoring seed-2 proposals share one Murcko core. The unseen feature needed to exceed the observed range cannot be identified from these examples.
Defined hydrazone geometry and a consistent choice among the hydroxy-aza-aromatic tautomeric possibilities are not established by the strings. No stereoisomer or tautomer comparison was supplied.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The amino-azine/nitrile maximum scores 0.6155870909 and the related butylamino heteroaryl analogue 0.6150075415. Four aromatic rings alone do not explain these values: the cited four-ring sulfone/sulfonamide assembly scores 0.3001508296, and an azine-family aryl methylsulfone variant scores 0.3476272862. Even the four-heavy-atom silicon-oxygen species receives 0.5004396377, so the numerical baseline is not a measure of medicinal-chemistry adequacy. Within late seed 2, a compact acylhydrazone scores 0.6018420613 while the extended repeated acylhydrazone scores 0.5758791436. The visible association is with particular aromatic attachment and heteroatom patterns; neither adding aromatic rings, nitriles, halogens nor molecular size is a universal rule.

per_task.generated_character: The high end contains recognizable amine-bearing medicinal chemistry, with more saturated carbon than the aromatic-amide and azine panels. Median size is 27 heavy atoms. Seed 0 produces aryl-oxypropyl piperidines and arylpiperazines with a second aromatic group, propyl substituents and halogens. The cited maximum has 28 heavy atoms, two benzene rings and a saturated piperazine ring, with an unacylated aliphatic nitrogen. Seed 1 uses alkyl-substituted indole arylpiperazines with N-benzyl substitution. Seed 2 develops hydroxyindolyl/aryl branched primary amines with ether-linked azetidine, pyrrolidine or piperidine groups; its cited leading late compounds have 29 heavy atoms and four rings. Ordinary ether formation and amine substitution make the main linkage patterns plausible, while branched stereogenic products need stereochemical control. The Parent also reached aryl-bearing cyclic amines, but had 357 amide-containing proposals versus 141 here and 153 piperazine-containing proposals versus 228 here. Its seed-2 maxima included N-hydroxyaminal-like connectivity; the current cited seed-2 maxima use primary amines instead. Current versus Parent maxima are 0.9999999801 versus 0.9961294199, 0.9999999417 versus 0.9999855105, and 0.9999998288 versus 0.9999832445.
liabilities: Alkylated, often halogenated aromatic groups linked by flexible chains to basic nitrogens raise lipophilicity, protonation and off-target questions. The neutral SMILES and low charged-text rate do not mean that the amines would remain neutral in solution.
Some late proposals grow additional aryl/amine appendages; size alone does not guarantee the same useful arrangement.
RDKit identifies unassigned tetrahedral centres in 362 of 870 accepted proposals versus 225 in the Parent. Neither panel provides explicit stereochemical notation.
missing_features: No necessary binding motif absent from the recorded maxima can be inferred: hydrophobic aromatic groups and unacylated cyclic amines are already present. Many low-scoring amide/sulfonamide structures lack that same nitrogen environment and spatial arrangement.

Defined stereochemistry is missing in the branched primary-amine family. The cited seed-2 maximum has an unassigned tetrahedral centre; the trajectories do not show which stereochemical form was intended.

The strongest seed-0 and seed-1 families offer limited alternative attachment geometries: their 58 highest-scoring proposals contain only 6 and 5 distinct Murcko cores respectively. Any chemical benefit from new geometries remains unmeasured at the observed score ceiling.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The aryl-oxypropyl piperazine reaches 0.9999999801. A similarly sized 25-heavy-atom, three-ring aryl-amide/thiadiazole molecule with a sulfonylated piperidine nitrogen scores 1.9828327576e-05. The nitro acylhydrazone scores 4.1105044112e-05. The association is with accessible unacylated amine centres and their spacing between aromatic groups, not nitrogen or ring count alone. An amine by itself is also insufficient: the late hydroxyphenethylamine scores 0.4396341729, below the branched indolyl/aryl amines near the reported ceiling. Numerous aryl F/Cl/I and substitution-position changes have essentially indistinguishable high scores. These saturated numerical values do not establish comparative binding affinity, selectivity or pharmacokinetic quality.

per_task.generated_character: The full output is broad: 735 distinct Murcko cores among 870 proposals, compared with 733 in the Parent, and a median of 23 heavy atoms and three rings. The seed-0 high end nevertheless repeatedly combines piperazine, aryl sulfonyl groups and a benzodioxole ring system, varying the second connection among sulfonamide, amide, carbamate, urea and amidine. Its cited maximum is a 27-heavy-atom bis(arylsulfonyl)piperazine with four rings, two aromatic. Both piperazine nitrogens are sulfonylated, so counting a piperazine here must not be confused with the unacylated basic-amine environment seen elsewhere. Another high example joins a fused nitrogen-containing lactam ring system to a sulfonylpiperazine and benzodioxole, with 35 heavy atoms and six rings. Seed 1 remains dispersed around benzodioxole/indole and sulfonylpiperazine chemistry; seed 2 includes aryl sulfonamides with methylpiperazine and fused lactams. Most leading amide and sulfonamide connections look synthetically conventional. Current versus Parent maxima are 0.241016 versus 0.212512, 0.192772 versus 0.204283, and 0.199800 versus 0.258869. The stronger Parent seed-2 molecule combined a benzodioxole sulfonylpiperazine with a fused aza-aromatic sulfonyl partner. The current seed-2 high end does not maintain that same assembled combination.
liabilities: Multiple sulfonyl groups and carbonyls create a substantial polar burden, while capping both piperazine nitrogens changes ionization relative to a free diamine. These consequences should not be inferred from nitrogen count alone.

One high digest member includes an unusual explicitly hydrogen-bearing sulfur centre bonded to oxo, aryl and nitrogen groups; its score of 0.2218238064 does not establish that connectivity as a stable synthetic product.
Simple acids, long-chain acyclic amines and unrelated polycyclic structures occupy the low-scoring tail despite the broad aggregate core count.
missing_features: The combined benzodioxole, aryl-sulfonyl and diamine-ring arrangement seen in the strongest examples is not consistently carried into the broad remaining output. Generating more unrelated rings has not supplied that missing co-occurrence.

Alternative fused heteroaromatic partners and polar-linker arrangements that retain the useful assembled context remain uneven across seeds. The Parent comparison shows that this chemistry was reachable, but does not establish a required target fragment.
Defined stereochemistry is absent from the saturated and bridged-ring excursions; the cited late bicyclic diketone has five unassigned tetrahedral centres.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The bis-sulfonylpiperazine scores 0.2410164257, the aromatic amide/sulfonamide 0.2318094739, and the urea/sulfonamide 0.2263778191. Glycolic acid and phosphoric acid score 0.0116405049 and 0.0082655920, and the acyclic aminonitrile scores 0.0134271539. The data favor organized aromatic and polar-linker combinations over small acids or isolated amines. Ring presence is still insufficient: the final saturated bicyclic diketone scores 0.0841158231 and a methoxyphenyl bridged amine 0.1174440439, whereas the fused aryl-sulfonamide lactam scores 0.1815338686. A 35-heavy-atom fused heteroaromatic example reaches 0.2402649305, so a simple smaller-is-better reading would also be wrong. The observed gradient depends on combining aromatic decoration with the appropriate polar connections.

per_task.generated_character: The output is chemically diverse rather than a single collapsed family: 783 distinct Murcko cores among 870 accepted proposals, versus 775 in the Parent. Median size is 24 heavy atoms with three rings. Seed 1 supplies the highest cited product, a 23-heavy-atom aryl sulfonamide on a benzo-fused O,N lactam, and a similarly compact aza/thio heteroaromatic ester. Seed 0 reaches a 23-heavy-atom tertiary aniline bearing benzyl nitrile, methoxyethyl and carboxamide substituents, as well as a spiro cyclic sulfonamide carboxylic acid and a trifluoromethyl alcohol/hydroxamate. Seed 2 reaches a 21-heavy-atom brominated quinolone-like nucleoside and an amide-linked piperidine/azine structure. These differ substantially in basicity and polarity; a common target-like scaffold is not visible. Conventional functional groups coexist with demanding spiro, glycosidic and stereogenic structures. Current versus Parent maxima are 0.186297 versus 0.271145, 0.192839 versus 0.264242, and 0.128520 versus 0.326097. The Parent high end included compact guanidine-bearing, thiourea/carbonyl and fluoro/trifluoromethyl sulfonyl-amide structures; the current high end does not reproduce that exact chemistry. The Parent and current better examples nevertheless occupy broadly similar compact size ranges, so broad scaffold availability alone does not explain the difference.
liabilities: Long alkyl chains, repeated peptide-like connections and oversized densely oxygenated polycycles consume substantial chemical complexity while scoring at or near zero.

Hydroxamates, sulfoxide representations, glycosidic linkages and stereogenic spiro or branched products require individual stability, speciation and synthesis assessment; their presence alone does not make them unsuitable.
There are 332 accepted proposals with unassigned tetrahedral centres, versus 274 in the Parent, with no explicit stereochemical notation in either panel.
missing_features: A reproducible compact polar arrangement is missing from most later products: isolated successful amide, sulfonamide, ether and amine combinations are followed by oversized or differently connected products. Size control alone would not repair the equally compact low-scoring examples.

The output lacks consistent stereochemical identity where it matters structurally: the cited glycosidic compound has three unassigned tetrahedral centres, and the spiro acid and alcohol/hydroxamate each have one. No stereochemical score preference can be inferred.

The molecules do not reveal a single absent target motif. The defensible gap is context-sensitive assembly of size, ring content and polar groups, not a task-named template or indiscriminate addition of fluorine.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The compact aryl sulfonamide/lactam scores 0.1928392260 and the tertiary-aniline carboxamide 0.1862969146. A 44-heavy-atom long-alkyl aryl hydroxamate and a 55-heavy-atom peptide-like structure score exactly 0. Across seeds, the 58 highest-scoring proposals have median heavy-atom counts 23, 22 and 22; the corresponding lowest-scoring groups have medians 38, 30 and 31. The size association is strong, but appropriate polar connectivity is also needed: the final 23-heavy-atom indolyl thioimidic structure scores 6.3468645426e-08, while a different 23-heavy-atom amino-azine scores 0.0468234245. The digest median of 0.0 is rounded; the exact median over all supplied records is 3.8150477172e-08, and only three accepted optimizer proposals score exactly zero. The late seed-2 set therefore represents continued chemically varied low-scoring output, not convergence onto the isolated compact maxima. No uniquely required fluorination pattern or basic amine can be inferred, since the leading cited sulfonamide/lactam is unfluorinated and lacks an unacylated aliphatic amine.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The cited compact aryl sulfonamide/lactam and tertiary-aniline carboxamide each have 23 heavy atoms and observed scores 0.1928392260 and 0.1862969146, while the 44-heavy-atom long-alkyl hydroxamate and 55-heavy-atom peptide-like product score 0. Elsewhere, a 24-heavy-atom diaryl cyanoacrylamide reaches 0.4952605565 while a 59-heavy-atom repeated indole-amide product falls to 2.7846374431e-48. Yet the compact 23-heavy-atom indolyl thioimidic example also scores only 6.3468645426e-08. Both scale and the way polar groups are connected matter.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently preserve a useful molecular size and polar-group context while constructing new structures.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The missing capability is to vary scaffold and attachment patterns while retaining the useful size, heteroatom environment and degree of substitution evidenced by accepted feedback. This calls for composition-sensitive growth and termination without imposing a universal desired size, fixed scaffold or objective identity.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The complete output contains hundreds of distinct Murcko cores in each panel, yet 53 of 58 high-scoring proposals in one diaryl activated-alkene seed and 57 of 58 in one acylhydrazone seed share a single core. Seven cited activated-alkene maxima retain exactly the same score after positional or amide-to-imidate changes. In contrast, broad low-scoring streams repeatedly lose the combined aromatic and polar-linker arrangement of their stronger examples.
transferable_gaps.gap: Broad ring availability does not translate into consistent exploration of alternative structures around productive chemical arrangements.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A transferable generator should be able both to preserve meaningful relationships between rings, linkers and polar groups and to change their topology beyond terminal substitution. The needed capability is context-preserving structural variation; core diversity or canonical novelty alone should not stand in for useful chemistry.

transferable_gaps.evidence: A cited 28-heavy-atom aryl-oxypropyl piperazine with an unacylated nitrogen scores 0.9999999801, while a 25-heavy-atom three-ring structure with sulfonylated piperidine nitrogen scores 1.9828327576e-05. Elsewhere, a bis-sulfonylpiperazine is itself a leading observed structure. Thus free amines, aromatic nitrogens, amides and sulfonamides are available, but their chemical roles are not interchangeable and there is no universal rule to add or unmask an amine.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator lacks reliable control over the functional role of nitrogen when it changes linkages and ring attachments.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: New structures need to preserve or deliberately vary nitrogen hybridization, adjacent electron-withdrawing groups and spacing from aromatic surfaces as distinct chemical features. Use each independent stream of accepted feedback to learn which arrangement transfers; do not infer ionization from formal charge notation or nitrogen count.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The digest includes aryl imidates, electrophilic cyanoacrylamides, acylhydrazones and repeated acylhydrazone extensions, plus an explicitly hydrogen-bearing hypervalent sulfur centre. Some have high observed scores, and the imidate even ties ordinary amide analogues. Their scores and successful RDKit parsing supply no synthesis or stability evidence.
transferable_gaps.gap: Valence-valid generation does not consistently distinguish conventional stable linkage patterns from reactive or unusual alternatives.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The missing chemical capability is to produce sensible functional-group connectivity and plausible alternative linkages while preserving useful surrounding context. Chemical feasibility should be distinguished from representation validity and high accepted score, without treating every occurrence of a legitimate reactive functional group as automatically unacceptable.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every digest stereocentre-notation rate is 0.0. Passive inspection also finds no slash/backslash double-bond geometry notation anywhere in either complete panel. The current accepted sets contain 108, 75, 362, 217 and 332 molecules with unassigned tetrahedral centres in the fixed panel order. Cited examples include a branched primary amine with one centre, a glycosidic structure with three and a bicyclic diketone with five; the activated alkenes and hydrazones also leave geometry unspecified.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator emits potentially stereogenic structures without specifying their stereochemical identity.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The absent capability is to represent and preserve intentional tetrahedral and double-bond stereochemistry when generating such structures. This enables chemically defined alternatives from ordinary feedback; it does not justify assuming that a particular stereoisomer would improve an unmeasured score.

method_name: Augmented Hill-Climb with a corpus-trained SMILES policy
method_thesis: Train a compact autoregressive SMILES prior solely on the supplied unlabeled corpus, then initialize a fresh policy from that prior for each objective. Use the initial observations and each subsequent scored batch to update only its highest-reward sequences with the Augmented Hill-Climb loss: fit policy log likelihood to frozen-prior log likelihood plus scaled observed reward. Sample complete molecules token by token from the updated policy, canonicalize them, and refill invalid or duplicate proposals by further generation. The corpus supplies language training, never a ranked molecular pool. Elite-conditioned policy updates should shift generation toward new high-scoring molecular combinations quickly enough to improve the benchmark's mean final Top-1. This is a small-budget transfer hypothesis, not a claim that published larger-budget gains carry over. The root uses the current scored batch; randomized historical replay is reserved for the first improvement. approach.method_basis: The Parent learns a recurrent SMILES language model from an unlabeled molecular corpus and starts each objective with a fresh policy copied from that frozen prior. A memory retains the thirty-two strongest earlier elites, and the strongest eligible historical records join the current examples with their original strings and scores. Within history, an example's weight decreases with the number of earlier fitting batches that used it. The total current and historical loss shares remain proportional to their row counts. The policy fits weighted squared errors toward frozen-prior log likelihood plus sixty times accepted reward, takes up to twelve clipped Adam steps, and retains the final policy. approach.novelty: Add gradient-norm balancing between the current and historical learning groups. Set the two loss shares inversely to those gradient norms, then hold the shares fixed for the update. Each group therefore starts with the same gradient contribution magnitude, while history keeps its existing relative weights. The measured Parent usually lets the current group dominate despite stronger historical rewards. Earlier siblings changed which histories train, their within-group exposure weights, residual penalties, target ceilings, checkpoint retention or historical displacement protection. This mechanism changes the balance between the two group gradients before the unchanged optimizer acts. Equal contribution does not guarantee useful historical information: it can greatly reduce learning from fresh molecules or reinforce repetition. finding_summary.headline: Balancing changed learning, but group-gradient reconstruction failed and every seed lost final score.
finding_summary.insights:
The first historical intervention isolates a useful tradeoff before the sampled trajectories diverge. On identical starting examples and likelihoods, average final current-group error was 41.85 with balancing versus 29.32 with the Parent, while historical error was 18.88 versus 23.33. Current fitting was worse in thirteen of fifteen matched sessions. More historical influence can therefore buy better average historical fitting while weakening learning from the fresh batch; it is not a general protection guarantee. Across the later child stream, historical group error still rose in 71 updates and 817 individual historical exposures worsened. History received more than 99% of the loss in 21 nonterminal updates, and the effective selected batch shrank from 9.19 to 5.82 rows on the same selected inputs.

The score loss is not explained by a universal absence of chemical variety. Accepted core counts fell for three objectives but rose slightly for median-2 and sitagliptin. The molecular assessment finds that sitagliptin remains broadly diverse while failing to reproduce useful compact polar arrangements consistently; its largest score loss occurs despite 783 distinct cores versus 775 before. Docking already reaches coherent cyclic-amine chemistry near the numerical ceiling. Familiar rings, higher validity and improved replay fitting do not by themselves produce useful new molecular combinations. The same recurrent representation still generates oversized tails, questionable linkages and unspecified stereochemistry. Positive, unattainable historical targets also remain common: 627 exposures versus 489 in the Parent, on their different sampled streams.

This rules out failure to change coefficients or gradient direction as the explanation for lost utility. It also shows that scalar balance is an insufficient success criterion. Exact group-vector reconstruction remains open: real backward agreement establishes which objective executed, but cannot explain the systematic disagreement with the separately summed gradients. The saved evidence cannot determine whether that numerical discrepancy contributed to the score loss. Any interpretation that stronger historical influence is beneficial must now account for both the observed loss of fresh-batch fitting and increased repetition, as well as this unresolved numerical behavior.
finding_summary.results:
The fixed-share mechanism reached the real optimizer. In all 420 history updates followed by proposals, the measured starting contribution imbalance fell from 0.7012 on average to at most 4.59e-8. History received 84.54% of the loss mass on average. Every update changed the direct gradient direction even after clipping, and all 450 real first backward passes matched the direct actual objective exactly. Original accepted targets, selected-member rules, within-history exposure ratios and the fifteen history-free first-proposal controls remained intact.

One registered numerical check failed systematically: the direct balanced gradient did not reconstruct from the separately measured group gradients within the stated tolerance in any of the 435 history updates. Relative discrepancies reached 0.283% in nonterminal updates and 0.413% in terminal updates, compared with the approximately 0.001% registered tolerance. This limits the claim of exact vector reconstruction; it does not erase the observed scalar balance, changed direct gradient or real optimizer execution.

After history fitting, raw duplicate draws increased from 37.38% to 57.67%, canonical-novel yield fell from 54.80% to 37.62%, and batches needing further sampling increased from 29 to 90. All fifteen evaluations nevertheless completed their 300-call budgets. Mean final Top-1 fell from 0.517655 to 0.493672, a paired change of -0.023983. Seed changes were -0.004895, -0.009276 and -0.057779. The largest task loss was sitagliptin, whose mean endpoint fell from 0.287161 to 0.169219. Mean recorded AUC rose from 0.406769 to 0.423980, mainly alongside faster docking progress, so better average early discovery did not deliver the predicted final-score gain.

finding_summary.headline: Balancing changed learning, but group-gradient reconstruction failed and every seed lost final score.
finding_summary.insights:
The first historical intervention isolates a useful tradeoff before the sampled trajectories diverge. On identical starting examples and likelihoods, average final current-group error was 41.85 with balancing versus 29.32 with the Parent, while historical error was 18.88 versus 23.33. Current fitting was worse in thirteen of fifteen matched sessions. More historical influence can therefore buy better average historical fitting while weakening learning from the fresh batch; it is not a general protection guarantee. Across the later child stream, historical group error still rose in 71 updates and 817 individual historical exposures worsened. History received more than 99% of the loss in 21 nonterminal updates, and the effective selected batch shrank from 9.19 to 5.82 rows on the same selected inputs.

The score loss is not explained by a universal absence of chemical variety. Accepted core counts fell for three objectives but rose slightly for median-2 and sitagliptin. The molecular assessment finds that sitagliptin remains broadly diverse while failing to reproduce useful compact polar arrangements consistently; its largest score loss occurs despite 783 distinct cores versus 775 before. Docking already reaches coherent cyclic-amine chemistry near the numerical ceiling. Familiar rings, higher validity and improved replay fitting do not by themselves produce useful new molecular combinations. The same recurrent representation still generates oversized tails, questionable linkages and unspecified stereochemistry. Positive, unattainable historical targets also remain common: 627 exposures versus 489 in the Parent, on their different sampled streams.

This rules out failure to change coefficients or gradient direction as the explanation for lost utility. It also shows that scalar balance is an insufficient success criterion. Exact group-vector reconstruction remains open: real backward agreement establishes which objective executed, but cannot explain the systematic disagreement with the separately summed gradients. The saved evidence cannot determine whether that numerical discrepancy contributed to the score loss. Any interpretation that stronger historical influence is beneficial must now account for both the observed loss of fresh-batch fitting and increased repetition, as well as this unresolved numerical behavior.

The fixed-share mechanism reached the real optimizer. In all 420 history updates followed by proposals, the measured starting contribution imbalance fell from 0.7012 on average to at most 4.59e-8. One registered numerical check failed systematically: the direct balanced gradient did not reconstruct from the separately measured group gradients within the stated tolerance in any of the 435 history updates. Relative discrepancies reached 0.283% in nonterminal updates and 0.413% in terminal updates, compared with the approximately 0.001% registered tolerance. finding_summary.headline: Balancing changed learning, but group-gradient reconstruction failed and every seed lost final score.
finding_summary.insights:
The first historical intervention isolates a useful tradeoff before the sampled trajectories diverge. On identical starting examples and likelihoods, average final current-group error was 41.85 with balancing versus 29.32 with the Parent, while historical error was 18.88 versus 23.33. Current fitting was worse in thirteen of fifteen matched sessions. More historical influence can therefore buy better average historical fitting while weakening learning from the fresh batch; it is not a general protection guarantee. Across the later child stream, historical group error still rose in 71 updates and 817 individual historical exposures worsened. History received more than 99% of the loss in 21 nonterminal updates, and the effective selected batch shrank from 9.19 to 5.82 rows on the same selected inputs.

The score loss is not explained by a universal absence of chemical variety. Accepted core counts fell for three objectives but rose slightly for median-2 and sitagliptin. The molecular assessment finds that sitagliptin remains broadly diverse while failing to reproduce useful compact polar arrangements consistently; its largest score loss occurs despite 783 distinct cores versus 775 before. Docking already reaches coherent cyclic-amine chemistry near the numerical ceiling. Familiar rings, higher validity and improved replay fitting do not by themselves produce useful new molecular combinations. The same recurrent representation still generates oversized tails, questionable linkages and unspecified stereochemistry. Positive, unattainable historical targets also remain common: 627 exposures versus 489 in the Parent, on their different sampled streams.

This rules out failure to change coefficients or gradient direction as the explanation for lost utility. It also shows that scalar balance is an insufficient success criterion. Exact group-vector reconstruction remains open: real backward agreement establishes which objective executed, but cannot explain the systematic disagreement with the separately summed gradients. The saved evidence cannot determine whether that numerical discrepancy contributed to the score loss. Any interpretation that stronger historical influence is beneficial must now account for both the observed loss of fresh-batch fitting and increased repetition, as well as this unresolved numerical behavior.
finding_summary.results:
The fixed-share mechanism reached the real optimizer. In all 420 history updates followed by proposals, the measured starting contribution imbalance fell from 0.7012 on average to at most 4.59e-8. History received 84.54% of the loss mass on average. Every update changed the direct gradient direction even after clipping, and all 450 real first backward passes matched the direct actual objective exactly. Original accepted targets, selected-member rules, within-history exposure ratios and the fifteen history-free first-proposal controls remained intact.

One registered numerical check failed systematically: the direct balanced gradient did not reconstruct from the separately measured group gradients within the stated tolerance in any of the 435 history updates. Relative discrepancies reached 0.283% in nonterminal updates and 0.413% in terminal updates, compared with the approximately 0.001% registered tolerance. This limits the claim of exact vector reconstruction; it does not erase the observed scalar balance, changed direct gradient or real optimizer execution.

After history fitting, raw duplicate draws increased from 37.38% to 57.67%, canonical-novel yield fell from 54.80% to 37.62%, and batches needing further sampling increased from 29 to 90. All fifteen evaluations nevertheless completed their 300-call budgets. Mean final Top-1 fell from 0.517655 to 0.493672, a paired change of -0.023983. Seed changes were -0.004895, -0.009276 and -0.057779. The largest task loss was sitagliptin, whose mean endpoint fell from 0.287161 to 0.169219. Mean recorded AUC rose from 0.406769 to 0.423980, mainly alongside faster docking progress, so better average early discovery did not deliver the predicted final-score gain.

molecular_assessment.headline: Ring-rich aromatic chemistry reaches coherent cyclic amines, but retains narrow analogue families, oversized tails and unspecified stereochemistry.
molecular_assessment.overall_character: This assessment reads every supplied trajectory for node n-95c3f5710341 and Parent n-3462511d7ff0: all five objectives and seeds 0, 1 and 2, with 900 recorded molecules and 870 accepted optimizer proposals per objective in each panel. No objective lacks trajectories. The counters describe accepted optimizer strings, not rejected raw generations or experimentally isolated compounds. In the fixed task order, ring-closure presence rates are 0.9977, 0.9966, 0.9954, 0.9908 and 0.9839; aromatic-atom presence rates are 0.9885, 0.9943, 0.9885, 0.9575 and 0.9425. These are molecule-level text-presence rates, not fractions of atoms that are aromatic. A passive RDKit reading gives median heavy-atom counts of 24, 32, 27, 23 and 24 and median ring counts of 3, 4, 4, 3 and 3. Phenyl and heteroaromatic rings, amides, sulfonamides, ethers, nitriles and saturated nitrogen heterocycles are all represented. Distinct atom/bond-specific Bemis-Murcko core counts are 425, 315, 506, 735 and 783, versus Parent counts 472, 372, 537, 733 and 775. Thus the complete output is structurally broad, while several high-scoring seed streams concentrate on close analogues. Core counts do not measure usefulness. Many leading structures use conventional medicinal-chemistry bonds, but imidates, activated alkenes, acylhydrazones, unusual sulfur connectivity, overgrown peptide-like structures and long alkyl appendages make the whole set only questionably plausible. All accepted structures parse in the matching RDKit environment; that establishes representation validity, not synthesis, stability, exposure or biological activity. Explicit tetrahedral and double-bond stereochemical notation is absent throughout both panels despite potentially stereogenic structures. Passive descriptor methods, source hashes and all seed comparisons are retained in runs/SPIRAL2/policy/responses/r0011-09-improve-L03-molecular-audit/audit.json and stereo.json. Score interpretations below are associations within the supplied molecules; they do not infer an unseen target structure or mechanism activation.

per_task.generated_character: The accepted set is dominated by compact aromatic amides: median 24 heavy atoms, with nitriles in 255 of 870 proposals versus 7 in the Parent. Seed 1 develops diaryl cyanoacrylamides with acetanilide or imidate substituents. Its cited maximum has 24 heavy atoms, two benzene rings, two carbonyls and a nitrile. Seed 0 instead reaches an N-ethyl methylpyrazole carboxamide attached to fluorobiphenyl, also with 24 heavy atoms, and related heteroaromatic lactam/carboxamides. Seed 2 keeps methoxy-substituted indole and benzimidazole families carrying an aryl amide or benzyl nitrile. These are recognizable small-molecule frameworks, although the imidates and activated alkene require more chemical scrutiny than ordinary aryl amides. The Parent maxima were predominantly three-ring pyrrole, aryl-ether and diarylamine carboxamides. Current versus Parent recorded maxima by seed are 0.492632 versus 0.490235, 0.495261 versus 0.447421, and 0.447848 versus 0.476731. The chemistry changes differently in each seed rather than uniformly acquiring a missing ring class.
liabilities: The cyanoacrylamide is an electrophilic conjugated alkene, and aryl imidates introduce hydrolytic and tautomeric questions. These are structural concerns, not measured reactivity or stability.
Repeated amide-rich growth, a permanently charged bulky peptide-like molecule and densely functionalized polycycles create large synthetic and physicochemical burdens.
There are 108 accepted proposals with RDKit-perceived unassigned tetrahedral centres, while the digest stereocentre-notation rate is 0.0.
missing_features: Consistent preservation of the compact aromatic, nitrogen-containing envelope is missing from the low-scoring tail; both excessive growth and nitrogen-free fragments occur. The data do not establish an obligatory unseen fused-ring scaffold.

Productive variation beyond the repeated diaryl activated-alkene core is limited within seed 1: 53 of its 58 highest-scoring accepted proposals share one atom/bond-specific Murcko core. Ring chemistry is available, but useful alternative attachment arrangements are unevenly explored.

Defined alkene geometry is missing from the cyanoacrylamides; defined tetrahedral stereochemistry is missing from more complex off-family products. The score evidence does not establish a benefit from specifying either.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The cited 24-heavy-atom acetanilide/cyanoacrylamide reaches 0.4952605565, whereas a 50-heavy-atom quaternary-ammonium peptide-like proposal scores 0 and the 59-heavy-atom repeated indole-amide/guanidine structure scores 2.7846374431e-48. Compactness is associated with the better observations, but is not sufficient: the nitrogen-free, 16-heavy-atom cyclic alcohol scores only 0.0107671849. Seven digest maxima score identically despite aryl positional changes and replacement of an acetanilide linkage by an imidate. This suggests limited discrimination among those compositionally similar arrangements, not evidence that the imidate has equal chemical quality. The initial trimethoxyindole carboxamide scores 0.3051048084; late seed-2 benzimidazole/benzyl-nitrile and related indole-amide examples score 0.4355405789 and 0.3410994870. A ring-rich but enlarged 33-heavy-atom late product drops to 5.3229519627e-06. The observed gradient favors a compact aromatic heteroatom/carbonyl arrangement over indiscriminate ring or chain growth.

per_task.generated_character: These are the largest typical proposals in the panel: median 32 heavy atoms and four aromatic rings, with halogen text in 0.7138 of accepted strings. Seed 0 builds four-ring amino-azine/heteroaryl systems with benzylamine links, aryl nitriles and sometimes trifluoromethyl groups. The maximum is a 33-heavy-atom triazine-bearing structure with nine nitrogen atoms, including three nitriles, and no oxygen. Seed 1 develops extensively substituted quinoline/oxazole/aryl ethers. Seed 2 instead concentrates on methoxy/hydroxy aza-aromatic acylhydrazones carrying fluorinated or brominated benzoyl groups. The final cited examples in that seed have three aromatic rings and 32-38 heavy atoms. The azine, ether and amide linkages are conventionally accessible in principle; multiple regioselective substitutions and acylhydrazone geometry complicate that general plausibility. Compared with the Parent, nitrile-bearing proposals rise from 31 to 214 and sulfonamides fall from 160 to 19. The Parent seed-0 high end included extended alternating nitrogen linkages; its seed-1 high end was also an amino-azine family, and seed 2 used aryl sulfonamides with imine-bearing extensions. Current versus Parent maxima are 0.615587 versus 0.589985, 0.607304 versus 0.618622, and 0.605208 versus 0.608588.
liabilities: Large aromatic surfaces, multiple halogens and closely related nitrile-rich substituent patterns can create solubility and selectivity concerns; neither property was measured here.
Acylhydrazones bring possible E/Z mixtures and hydrolytic sensitivity, and some products repeat that linkage rather than introducing a distinct stable framework.
The low-scoring thiocarbonyl-to-sulfone linkage and isolated silicon-oxygen fragment illustrate that a valid representation can still be chemically unusual for this molecular context.
missing_features: The most productive amino-azine and aryl-nitrile arrangement is absent from the lower-scoring sulfone-rich examples, despite similar aromatic ring content. Ring count alone misses the relevant attachment chemistry.

Alternative coherent linkers and ring connectivities are poorly represented within the late acylhydrazone family: 57 of the 58 highest-scoring seed-2 proposals share one Murcko core. The unseen feature needed to exceed the observed range cannot be identified from these examples.
Defined hydrazone geometry and a consistent choice among the hydroxy-aza-aromatic tautomeric possibilities are not established by the strings. No stereoisomer or tautomer comparison was supplied.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The amino-azine/nitrile maximum scores 0.6155870909 and the related butylamino heteroaryl analogue 0.6150075415. Four aromatic rings alone do not explain these values: the cited four-ring sulfone/sulfonamide assembly scores 0.3001508296, and an azine-family aryl methylsulfone variant scores 0.3476272862. Even the four-heavy-atom silicon-oxygen species receives 0.5004396377, so the numerical baseline is not a measure of medicinal-chemistry adequacy. Within late seed 2, a compact acylhydrazone scores 0.6018420613 while the extended repeated acylhydrazone scores 0.5758791436. The visible association is with particular aromatic attachment and heteroatom patterns; neither adding aromatic rings, nitriles, halogens nor molecular size is a universal rule.

per_task.generated_character: The high end contains recognizable amine-bearing medicinal chemistry, with more saturated carbon than the aromatic-amide and azine panels. Median size is 27 heavy atoms. Seed 0 produces aryl-oxypropyl piperidines and arylpiperazines with a second aromatic group, propyl substituents and halogens. The cited maximum has 28 heavy atoms, two benzene rings and a saturated piperazine ring, with an unacylated aliphatic nitrogen. Seed 1 uses alkyl-substituted indole arylpiperazines with N-benzyl substitution. Seed 2 develops hydroxyindolyl/aryl branched primary amines with ether-linked azetidine, pyrrolidine or piperidine groups; its cited leading late compounds have 29 heavy atoms and four rings. Ordinary ether formation and amine substitution make the main linkage patterns plausible, while branched stereogenic products need stereochemical control. The Parent also reached aryl-bearing cyclic amines, but had 357 amide-containing proposals versus 141 here and 153 piperazine-containing proposals versus 228 here. Its seed-2 maxima included N-hydroxyaminal-like connectivity; the current cited seed-2 maxima use primary amines instead. Current versus Parent maxima are 0.9999999801 versus 0.9961294199, 0.9999999417 versus 0.9999855105, and 0.9999998288 versus 0.9999832445.
liabilities: Alkylated, often halogenated aromatic groups linked by flexible chains to basic nitrogens raise lipophilicity, protonation and off-target questions. The neutral SMILES and low charged-text rate do not mean that the amines would remain neutral in solution.
Some late proposals grow additional aryl/amine appendages; size alone does not guarantee the same useful arrangement.
RDKit identifies unassigned tetrahedral centres in 362 of 870 accepted proposals versus 225 in the Parent. Neither panel provides explicit stereochemical notation.
missing_features: No necessary binding motif absent from the recorded maxima can be inferred: hydrophobic aromatic groups and unacylated cyclic amines are already present. Many low-scoring amide/sulfonamide structures lack that same nitrogen environment and spatial arrangement.

Defined stereochemistry is missing in the branched primary-amine family. The cited seed-2 maximum has an unassigned tetrahedral centre; the trajectories do not show which stereochemical form was intended.

The strongest seed-0 and seed-1 families offer limited alternative attachment geometries: their 58 highest-scoring proposals contain only 6 and 5 distinct Murcko cores respectively. Any chemical benefit from new geometries remains unmeasured at the observed score ceiling.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The aryl-oxypropyl piperazine reaches 0.9999999801. A similarly sized 25-heavy-atom, three-ring aryl-amide/thiadiazole molecule with a sulfonylated piperidine nitrogen scores 1.9828327576e-05. The nitro acylhydrazone scores 4.1105044112e-05. The association is with accessible unacylated amine centres and their spacing between aromatic groups, not nitrogen or ring count alone. An amine by itself is also insufficient: the late hydroxyphenethylamine scores 0.4396341729, below the branched indolyl/aryl amines near the reported ceiling. Numerous aryl F/Cl/I and substitution-position changes have essentially indistinguishable high scores. These saturated numerical values do not establish comparative binding affinity, selectivity or pharmacokinetic quality.

per_task.generated_character: The full output is broad: 735 distinct Murcko cores among 870 proposals, compared with 733 in the Parent, and a median of 23 heavy atoms and three rings. The seed-0 high end nevertheless repeatedly combines piperazine, aryl sulfonyl groups and a benzodioxole ring system, varying the second connection among sulfonamide, amide, carbamate, urea and amidine. approach.method_basis: The Parent learns a recurrent SMILES language model from an unlabeled molecular corpus and starts each objective with a fresh policy copied from that frozen prior. Each accepted batch contributes its best-scoring half. A memory retains the thirty-two strongest earlier elites, and the strongest eligible historical records join the current examples with their original strings and scores. Within history, an example's weight decreases with the number of earlier fitting batches that used it. The total current and historical loss shares remain proportional to their row counts. The policy fits weighted squared errors toward frozen-prior log likelihood plus sixty times accepted reward, takes up to twelve clipped Adam steps, and retains the final policy. It directly samples complete SMILES, with chemical validation and canonical duplicate rejection refilling each batch.
approach.novelty: Add gradient-norm balancing between the current and historical learning groups. At the start of each history-bearing update, measure the current mean-loss gradient and the historical gradient after the Parent's exposure weighting. Set the two loss shares inversely to those gradient norms, then hold the shares fixed for the update. Each group therefore starts with the same gradient contribution magnitude, while history keeps its existing relative weights. The measured Parent usually lets the current group dominate despite stronger historical rewards. Earlier siblings changed which histories train, their within-group exposure weights, residual penalties, target ceilings, checkpoint retention or historical displacement protection. This mechanism changes the balance between the two group gradients before the unchanged optimizer acts. Equal contribution does not guarantee useful historical information: it can greatly reduce learning from fresh molecules or reinforce repetition. Actual gradient and proposal evidence will determine whether that tradeoff helps.
